## `spatial_similarity()`

Spatial similarity between spatial transcriptomics samples.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

```r
spatial_similarity(samples, normalize = TRUE, pools = NULL,
                   only_transitions = FALSE,
                   neighborhood = c("auto", "radius", "knn", "delaunay"),
                   radius = NULL, k = 6)
```

## Python

```python
spatial_similarity(samples, normalize=True, pools=None, only_transitions=False,
                   neighborhood="auto", radius=None, k=6)
```
:::

### Arguments

`samples`
: [Named list]{.lang-r}[Dict]{.lang-py} of [data frames]{.lang-r}[DataFrames]{.lang-py},
  one per sample, with columns: `x`, `y` (positions of spots/cells in any unit,
  e.g. pixels or micrometres, consistent between samples); `label` (e.g. cell
  type).

`normalize`
: Divide each sample's connection counts by their total to control for sample
  size.

`pools`
: Optional [named list]{.lang-r}[dict]{.lang-py} mapping pool names to
  [sample names]{.lang-r}[lists of sample names]{.lang-py}; connection counts
  are summed within each pool, e.g.
  [`list(group_1 = c("sample_1", "sample_2"), group_2 = "sample_3")`]{.lang-r}[`{"group_1": ["sample_1", "sample_2"], "group_2": ["sample_3"]}`]{.lang-py}.

`only_transitions`
: If [`TRUE`]{.lang-r}[`True`]{.lang-py}, only count connections between spots
  with distinct labels (i.e. borders); does not count connections between
  spots with the same label.

`neighborhood`
: Definition of the neighbourhood of each spot/cell: `"radius"` selects all
  within `radius`; `"knn"` selects the `k` nearest (symmetric: both are
  included in each other's neighborhood if either is among the other's
  nearest); or `"delaunay"` selects those surrounding it by Delaunay
  triangulation, dropping links longer than `radius`. The default, `"auto"`,
  uses `"radius"` if the positions lie on a grid (at least 75% of
  nearest-neighbor distances within 10% of their median) and `"delaunay"`
  otherwise, with a message saying which was used.

`radius`
: Neighborhood radius for `"radius"`, or maximum link length for
  `"delaunay"`, in the units of `x` and `y`. By default, set from the spacing
  of the data: set to the median distance from each spot/cell to its nearest
  neighbor over all samples, multiplied by 1.2 for `"radius"` or 3 for
  `"delaunay"`. Used to make neighborhoods wider or narrower.

`k`
: Number of nearest neighbors for
  [`neighborhood = "knn"`]{.lang-r}[`neighborhood="knn"`]{.lang-py}. Ties are
  broken arbitrarily.

### Value

A symmetric [matrix]{.lang-r}[DataFrame]{.lang-py} of similarities, with rows
and columns named by sample (or pool) in input order. Similarities lie in
\[0, 1\]: 1 = identical, 0 = least similar pair. With
[`normalize = TRUE`]{.lang-r}[`normalize=True`]{.lang-py}, samples with no
neighbouring spots (or, with
[`only_transitions = TRUE`]{.lang-r}[`only_transitions=True`]{.lang-py}, no
neighbouring spots with different labels) get [`NA`]{.lang-r}[`NaN`]{.lang-py}.

### Details

Each sample is characterised in terms of the number of times labels neighbor
one another (e.g. how often a `Neuron` borders an `Astrocyte`). With
[`only_transitions = TRUE`]{.lang-r}[`only_transitions=True`]{.lang-py},
connections between identical labels are excluded. These connection counts form
one vector per sample, which is optionally pooled (across samples) and
normalised (within each sample, by its total). The similarity score between two
samples is given by `1 - (d / max(d))`, where `d` is the Euclidean distance
between two samples' vectors and `max(d)` is the maximum distance across all
pairs of samples/pools.

### Extracting positions

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## R

For a Seurat object `obj` from `Load10X_Spatial()` (Visium; or Visium HD,
with e.g. `bin.size = 8` for bins or `bin.size = "polygons"` for segmented
cells) or `LoadXenium()` (Xenium), with cell types in `obj$cell_type`:

```r
coords <- GetTissueCoordinates(obj)
df <- data.frame(x = coords$x, y = coords$y, label = obj$cell_type[coords$cell])
```

If an object holds several images, such as more than one bin size, choose one
with `image`, e.g. `GetTissueCoordinates(obj, image = "slice1.008um")`.

## Python

For Visium read with scanpy or squidpy, and for tables read with
[spatialdata-io](https://spatialdata.scverse.org/projects/io/) (Xenium's
`adata = sdata.tables["table"]`, or Visium HD bins' e.g.
`adata = sdata.tables["square_008um"]`), with cell types in
`adata.obs["cell_type"]`:

```python
x, y = adata.obsm["spatial"].T
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": x, "y": y, "label": adata.obs["cell_type"]})
```

For Visium HD segmented cells, `sdata.tables["cell_segmentations"]` has no
`obsm["spatial"]`, so take the centroids of the cells' outlines instead:

```python
adata = sdata.tables["cell_segmentations"]
cells = sdata.shapes[adata.obs["region"].iloc[0]].centroid.loc[adata.obs_names]
df = pd.DataFrame({"x": cells.x, "y": cells.y, "label": adata.obs["cell_type"]})
```
:::

### Neighbors

Under default settings, the neighbourhoods of each sample's spots/cells depend
on technology:

| Data | Neighborhood |
|---|---|
| Visium spots | Six immediate neighbors |
| Visium HD bins | Four side neighbors; set `radius` to 1.5 times the bin size to add the diagonals |
| Segmented cells (Xenium, or Visium HD with cell segmentation) | The cells surrounding them, ignoring links across gaps |

Positions can be the pixel or micrometre coordinates from Space Ranger or
Xenium outputs, as long as all samples use the same units. As the spacing is
taken over all samples, don't mix samples in different units or from different
technologies.

### Warnings

- Labels that are missing values ([`NA`]{.lang-r}[`NaN` or `None`]{.lang-py})
  are kept as a label called `"NA"`, with a warning. Files read with
  [`read.csv()`]{.lang-r}[`pd.read_csv()`]{.lang-py} turn text such as "NA"
  into missing values; read them with
  [`na.strings = character(0)`]{.lang-r}[`keep_default_na=False`]{.lang-py} to
  keep the text.
- With [`normalize = TRUE`]{.lang-r}[`normalize=True`]{.lang-py}, samples with
  no neighbouring spots (or, with
  [`only_transitions = TRUE`]{.lang-r}[`only_transitions=True`]{.lang-py}, no
  neighbouring spots with different labels) are named in a warning, and their
  similarities are [`NA`]{.lang-r}[`NaN`]{.lang-py}.
